title: Purana sona bechne par poora paisa kyun nahi milta?
hooks: Purana sona bechne ja rahe ho? Ye 3 galtiyan paisa kha jaati hain
Sona becha ₹50,000 ka, haath aaye ₹38,000? Jaano kyun
Gold exchange kiya naya kharidne ke liye? GST ka chakkar samjho
hook_why: Mistake warning pattern works best for gold topics (Indian Dollar 173k views with 'PURANE SONE...'), immediately relatable to anyone with old jewelry
metaphor: Receipt breaking down every deduction from gold weight to final cash — like a restaurant bill but each line shows what the jeweller keeps
mechanism: Purity test (XRF/BIS hallmark) decides karat percentage
Net weight = gross weight minus stones/solder (1-3% deduction)
Making charges paid while buying are NOT returned
GST only applies on new purchase/exchange difference, not on sale
Final payout = net gold weight × today's rate × purity %

claims.claim: BIS hallmarking mandatory for gold jewellery since 16 June 2021
claims.basis: BIS Hallmarking Regulations, Ministry of Consumer Affairs notification dated 16 Jun 2021

claims.claim: Making charges paid at purchase are not refunded when selling old gold
claims.basis: Gold Mart Jewellers guide 'Purana Sona Bechna Pune — GST, Purity aur Sahi Price Guide' and Anjaneya Gold Point blog

claims.claim: GST at 3% applies only on new jewellery purchase or exchange difference, not on outright sale of old gold
claims.basis: GST Council notifications; Gold Mart Jewellers guide confirms 'Jab aap purana sona bechte hain, GST aap pe nahi lagta'

claims.claim: Typical solder/impurity deduction is 1-3% of gross weight
claims.basis: Gold Mart Jewellers guide: 'Impurity / Solder Deduction... Typically 1–3% deducted'

claims.claim: Stone weight is separated and valued separately
claims.basis: Gold Mart Jewellers guide: 'Stone Weight... unka weight alag kiya jaata hai — stones ki alag valuation hoti hai'

claims.claim: Final payout = Net gold weight × Today's gold rate × Purity %
claims.basis: Gold Mart Jewellers guide formula: 'Final value = Net gold weight × Today's gold rate × Purity %'

steps_learned: Check for BIS hallmark before selling to avoid purity guesswork
Get purity tested via XRF machine (non-destructive) at the buyer's shop
Compare buy-back rates at 2–3 different jewellers
Understand making charges and solder/wastage deductions are never refunded
Distinguish between outright sale (no GST on seller) and exchange (3% GST on difference amount)
missing_steps: How XRF machine works and why it's more reliable than touchstone/acid test
Exact GST calculation: 3% on (new jewellery value – old gold credit) during exchange
BIS hallmark components (BIS logo, purity grade, jeweller's mark, year) and how to verify via BIS Care app
Formula: settlement weight = gross weight × (purity%/100) minus stones/non-gold parts
Making charges typically 8–14% of gold value; solder/wastage 1–2% extra
unsourced: Example numbers: 20 g 22K chain, making charges ₹8,000, solder ₹1,200
